newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt parliament passes new investment law.
newsitem.headline: Egypt parliament passes new investment law.

text.p: Egypt's parliament passed an investment law on Monday night to help attract capital to an ambitious scheme for a new community in the south of the country, parliamentary sources said on Tuesday.
Under the new law, investors in Toskha and the New Valley -- a pet project of President Hosni Mubarak -- would get a 20-year tax break.
Those investing in satellite cities, remote areas and the new industrial zones set up in recent years would get a 10-year tax exemption.

Other highlights of the law include cutting the lengthy bureaucratic procedures needed to set up business, and allowing the government to give land to investors who set up projects in sectors specified by the state.
These include land reclamation, hotels, cargo and silos, housing for rent, brokerage firms, and hospitals which provide free social services.

Mubarak appointed a new cabinet in 1996 to speed up economic reforms and Egypt has since tried to attract large amounts of foreign and local investment in the hope of becoming a regional "tiger" economy similar to those of South East Asian countries.

Investment-grade credit ratings and several conferences aimed at promoting investment opportunities have helped raise Egypt's profile. But investors have often complained of legal and bureaucratic setbacks. -- Cairo newsroom +202 578 3290/1
